answer_to: intern q-1 (#1261 async mechanism vs self-emit ordering)

ARCHAEOLOGY.INTRODUCED_BY: 320ed3e5 2026-06-26 'fix(forward): bridge ctx_search/ctx_fetch retrieval bytes to the platform' (cm-main, v1). No PR/issue number in the subject; this is the v1 fix REVIEW-r4a #4 cites.
ARCHAEOLOGY.ORIGINAL_INTENT: Commit body, quoted verbatim: 'bytes_retrieved ... was 0 across all 124,454 prod events ... Root cause: PostToolUse never fires for the plugin's OWN MCP tools, so the hook-side extractMcpToolCall path never observes ctx_search / ctx_fetch_and_index. ... Bridge the two processes through a tmp marker keyed by the session DB basename ... The server appends each retrieval's response byte count; the next ordinary-tool PostToolUse consumes the marker (consume-once) and emits a forwardable event carrying bytes_retrieved.' This is the self-emit mechanism: the server writes a marker, and the NEXT ordinary-tool PostToolUse call (a synchronous, in-order hook invocation) reads and clears it.
ARCHAEOLOGY.REGRESSION_RISK: The consume-once marker handshake assumes PostToolUse invocations are ordered and each runs to completion before the next tool's PreToolUse. #1261's proposed fix ('detached spawn, host does not wait on stdout' — BOTTLENECKS-r4.md:31, stated with 'e.g.,' as an example, not a decided mechanism) removes that guarantee: if PostToolUse becomes a fire-and-forget detached process, two hooks can run concurrently or out of order, and the marker can be consumed twice, consumed before the server finishes writing it, or left stale across session boundaries. That reopens 320ed3e5's exact bug (bytes_retrieved reads as 0 or wrong) in a new form — a race instead of a missing hook.
ARCHAEOLOGY.SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: BOTTLENECKS-r4.md:31's own fix text already states the needed constraint: 'keep index writes ordered before the next PreToolUse read.' Any async/detached PostToolUse dispatch for #1261 must preserve that same ordering for the marker read-then-clear step specifically — e.g. the marker consume step must still run synchronously (or be made atomic/idempotent) even if the rest of the hook body is dispatched async. Journal/index writes that are NOT consume-once (plain PostToolUse extraction) can be made async freely.

docGapDetail: TECH-SPEC.md:39,291,342 states a GS6/GP3 budget and 'PostToolUse async where host allows' but names no concrete mechanism (confirmed: BOTTLENECKS-r4 item 4 says this explicitly — 'written as a requirement with no concrete mechanism named'). 'Detached spawn, host does not wait on stdout' in BOTTLENECKS-r4.md:31 is offered with 'e.g.,' — an example fix suggestion from the review, not a decision recorded in DECISIONS-r3.md (Q1-Q19 do not cover #1261) and not yet written into TECH-SPEC or ADR-0009. Neither TECH-SPEC nor ADR-0009 says anything about ordering requirements between the self-emit marker handshake and any future async PostToolUse dispatch.
recommended_answer: 1. 'Detached spawn, host does not wait on stdout' is a reasonable mechanism to build for M0 (it is the standard way to stop the host blocking on hook stdout), but it is only a review suggestion right now, not a decided spec — TECH-SPEC/ADR-0009 must name it explicitly before GP3 can test it, per BOTTLENECKS-r4 item 4's own fix text. 2. The server-side self-emit path (320ed3e5's marker handshake, REVIEW-r4a #4) is NOT independent of the async dispatch change — both touch the same PostToolUse call. Build order: land the self-emit journal-write path FIRST (or at minimum design it so the marker-consume step is atomic/ordered on its own, not relying on 'the next PostToolUse runs synchronously'), THEN add the async/detached dispatch for the rest of the hook body. Doing it in the other order risks shipping the async change against the current synchronous-marker assumption and reopening the exact bytes_retrieved bug 320ed3e5 fixed, as a race condition instead of a missing call.
